cards.text: The whole congregation of Israel gathers in one place and sets up the Tent of Meeting there. EVERYBODY, in one spot. I spent years in a junk drawer, and even THAT didn't feel this crowded.

cards.question: Where does the whole congregation of Israel gather and set up the Tent of Meeting?

cards.text: The land is subdued before them, so the job's done, right? Not so fast, friend, because some tribes still haven't received their inheritance.

cards.question: ___ tribes of Israel still haven't received their inheritance.

cards.text: So Joshua, Israel's leader, stands up with a question for the Israelites.

cards.question: Seven tribes are still waiting on their land. What does Joshua ask the Israelites?

answers.text: How long they'll put off taking the land
Why they set up the Tent at Shiloh
Who will lead them after he dies

cards.text: Land the LORD, the God of their fathers, already GAVE them, and seven tribes are hitting the snooze button on it. So Joshua lays out a plan.

cards.question: Joshua tells the Israelites to appoint ___ men from each tribe.
What will Joshua send these men from each tribe out to do?

answers.text: Survey the land and map it out
Drive the Canaanites out of it
Build an altar in every region

cards.question: When the men come back to Joshua, they'll divide the land into seven portions.

cards.text: Joshua also mentions Judah and the house of Joseph. They won't be part of this, because they stay right where they are.

cards.question: Joshua says Judah stays in its territory in the north, and the house of Joseph stays in its territory in the south.
Once the seven portions are mapped out and brought to Joshua, how will he decide which tribe gets which?

answers.text: Give the biggest tribe first pick

cards.text: And there's more. Joshua says the Levites have no portion among them.

cards.question: The Levites have no portion of land, because their inheritance is the ___ of the LORD.
Gad, Reuben and half the tribe of Manasseh aren't in this drawing either, because they already received land from Moses beyond the Jordan to the east.

cards.text: As the men get up to go, Joshua tells them again to survey the land, map it out and come back, so he can cast lots for them here in Shiloh before the LORD. Friend, that's exactly how I explain a recipe: twice, and then once more while you're already mixing.
So off they go, all through the land, mapping it city by city into seven portions.

cards.question: When the men come back to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh, what do they bring with them?

answers.text: A count of every fighting man

cards.text: Then Joshua casts lots for them in the presence of the LORD at Shiloh and hands out the land. Friend, I haven't held my breath like this since my junk drawer days, when every time that drawer slid open, we all waited to see who'd get picked.

Then the lots come out one by one for Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Dan, each with its borders, cities and villages. Benjamin's cities include Jebus, that is, Jerusalem, and Simeon's land sits inside Judah's, because the share for Judah was too large for them. Yes, friend. THAT Jerusalem.

cards.question: When all the land is divided, the Israelites give one more inheritance to someone among them. Who?
The Israelites give Joshua his inheritance on their own, without any command from the LORD.
The Israelites give Joshua the city of Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. How does it end up being that city?

answers.text: It was the last city left

cards.question: Joshua ___ the city of Timnath-serah and settles in it.

cards.text: Eleazar the priest, Joshua and the heads of the families handed out all these inheritances by lot, right at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: All of these inheritances were handed out at Shiloh, before the LORD.

cards.text: So they finished dividing up the land. Seven tribes, seven lots, and not one argument in these two chapters. Friend, I once got into an argument with an oven timer. And I LOST.

findings.problem: The setup says only that the Levites have no portion. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out that their inheritance is the priesthood, so the blank asks for a key Bible word the baker has not seen rather than a meaning supported by context.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This is the first time Moses appears, but the question calls him only Moses and never says simply who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This non-opening story card runs to four sentences, including "Yes, friend." and "THAT Jerusalem."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Cards 2, 3 and 4 ask for facts that no earlier card supplies: who receives the final inheritance, whether the LORD commanded it, and how Timnath-serah was chosen. Three of the stop's five choice cards therefore depend on discovery or luck rather than reasoning, leaving most of its choices uninformed.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: "All of these inheritances" points back to the preceding story card without identifying the tribal inheritances or their distribution, so the question does not supply its own context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: The closing story card has four sentences rather than the permitted one or two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
